findings.finding: The three parts tell different return stories in every scenario. The core drivers imply a pre-tax return on new capital of mature_margin x sales_to_capital: bear 0.08 x 0.25 = 2.0%, base 0.17 x 0.35 = 6.0% (about 4.7% after tax), bull 0.25 x 0.45 = 11.3%. company_path asks the engine for ROIC of 6% / 12% / 20%, roughly 2-3x higher. The bull reason gets to 20% by using customer prepayments (about 55% of capex). But core.sales_to_capital already counts the same prepayments ('prepayments lower own capital per dollar of revenue: base 0.35'), so they are counted twice. The base path calls 12% 'slightly above the cost of capital', while the base drivers earn below any plausible NBIS cost of equity, so base growth destroys value in the DCF and creates value in the multiple path. No table price depends on it today because valuation was not computed, but every yearly price will depend on it once the repair pass makes the engine run.
findings.where: position/path.json company_path.scenarios.{bear,base,bull}.roic vs position/core.json drivers.mature_margin and drivers.sales_to_capital; position/coherence.md all three scenarios
findings.fix: Make one return per scenario. Either set path roic to the after-tax return the core drivers imply (about 1.6% / 4.7% / 8.9%), or raise the core margin or sales_to_capital with evidence so the two agree. Count prepayments once (in sales_to_capital, or as a funding line, not both), and state the cost of equity next to each roic.

findings.finding: Counter-thesis (pre-mortem, written 2029): NBIS grew revenue as planned, but every dollar of growth earned below its cost of capital, so shareholders lost money. How it happens: (1) GPU capacity is a commodity bought from the same supplier (NVIDIA) as CoreWeave and the hyperscalers. CoreWeave's operating margin went from 16.9% (FY2024) to -0.9% (FY2025) and -1.9% (Q2 2026) as depreciation and interest scaled, and NBIS follows the same curve. (2) Chips age on a 5-year book life that management just lengthened from 4 years (2026), so 2026-2027 earnings are flattered and the write-down comes when Vera Rubin cuts Blackwell rental prices. (3) The base case alone needs about (25.8B - 3.2B) / 0.35 = about 64B of new capital through FY2029 (on top of 20-25B of 2026 capex) against negative FCF (-3.6B in H1 even after 4.4B of prepayments). It is funded by convertibles, ATM sales at falling prices and a 364-day Citi facility, so the share count compounds. (4) 59% of Q2 revenue sits with three customers, and Meta and Microsoft hold service credits and tranche-termination rights on delays (understand/business.json), so one site slip (Vineland) turns into a lost tranche plus refunds of prepayments. Early signs to watch: the AI cloud adjusted EBITDA margin falling below 50% while connected MW rise; depreciation staying above about 40% of revenue after capacity is earning; auction or renewal prices below Blackwell levels after the Rubin launch; diluted share count up more than 15% a year; the Citi facility rolled at a wider spread or not rolled; any tranche termination or service-credit disclosure; CoreWeave bond yields (about 15%) not normalising.
findings.fix: Put this mechanism (return on new capital below the cost of capital, plus refinancing dilution) into the bear as drivers, not only as events. Add falsifiers for it (see the falsifier finding).

findings.finding: The bear does not size its own mechanisms. FY2027 revenue is still +110% (about 6.7B) while the bear events are a closed credit market, refinancing of a 364-day facility, a customer cut of 'up to a quarter of revenue' (the 24% customer) and a cut in GPU-hour prices. A closed credit market would stop the more-than-1-GW 2027 build, and a 24% customer loss on top of exit ARR below 7B points to FY2027 revenue near or below the 2026 exit run-rate. Dilution is the key risk, but forecast_options.financing is 'assumed': there is no share issuance, price or funding gap in the bear. The bear changes the margin and capital turns, but its growth and funding are close to management's plan.
findings.fix: Size each bear event. Customer loss = 24% of revenue from a dated quarter. Funding gap = capex plan minus OCF minus available facilities, giving shares issued at a stated discounted price. Credit closure = 2027 MW added cut to what is already funded. Then set bear FY2027 growth from that, and declare financing explicitly so redteam's funding check can run.

findings.finding: Several forensic flags never reach the bear or the risks. The risk register marks every high-severity item in_bear_case=false and 'not_priced': acc.beneish (M = 10.46), biz.customer_concentration, biz.moat, exe.external_funding and dil.sbc. The Piotroski 6/7 'strong' screen is false comfort and should not be read as quality. positive_net_income comes from the 780.6M ClickHouse revaluation gain, positive_operating_cash_flow comes from a 4,395M deferred-revenue build (customer prepayments, partly refundable), and no_new_shares=true contradicts the H1 2026 treasury share sales (2,846.7M), the ATM (12.7M shares) and the 2,000M NVIDIA pre-funded warrants. The ROIC series FY2020-FY2023 and the Altman Z'' 'safe' zone rest on the Yandex-era balance sheet and retained earnings, not the AI-cloud business.
findings.where: prefetch/forensic.json piotroski.signals, roic.series, altman; casefile.json rk.register (acc.beneish, biz.*, exe.external_funding, dil.sbc in_bear_case=false)
findings.fix: In position/core.json gaps or reasons, mark Piotroski, Altman and pre-2024 ROIC as not meaningful (non-operating gain, prepayment-driven OCF, share issuance missed, Yandex-era base). Explain or size the Beneish components (DSRI 12.19, LVGI 5.15 from the divestiture and the debt build). Tie customer concentration, funding/dilution and SBC (74.9M a quarter) to bear drivers so the register shows them as priced.

findings.finding: Guardrail: prepayment cash is treated as shareholders' cash. Cash of 9.3B (and H1 OCF of 4.5B) includes customer prepayments that are deferred revenue, partly refundable, with service credits and tranche termination on delivery delays. They fund capex owed to those customers and are not spendable cash for equity holders, much like insurance float counted as cash. The net-cash bridge subtracts debt only. The bull also counts the same prepayments as a reason for a 20% return.
findings.where: casefile.json qa.fields.cash_and_liquid_investments; rv.mechanical.redteam.reported.cash_and_equivalents; understand/business.json (refundable prepayments note); position/path.json scenarios.bull.reason_he
findings.fix: Show the refundable or unearned portion of deferred revenue as a claim in the capital bridge (or show prepayment-funded capex as committed), and keep spendable cash separate. Use prepayments once, as funding, in the drivers.

findings.finding: What the price assumes could not be tested. The red team returned unable_to_verify, with its critical checks revenue_basis, reinvestment and funding undeclared, and no expectation_gap ran because there is no valuation and no capital structure. A rough reviewer check: 155.69 x 271.9M shares (2026-06-30, before the ATM remainder, the NVIDIA warrants and the August converts) is about 42B of equity. The base FY2029 revenue path (9.6B x 1.85 x 1.45, about 25.8B) at a 17% margin gives about 4.4B of EBIT before interest on 8.5B+ of debt and before dilution from about 64B of required capital. So the price needs the base revenue path and a margin CoreWeave earned in only one year, plus funding without heavy dilution. In the bear (about 10B revenue x 8%) operating income barely covers interest.
findings.where: casefile.json rv.mechanical.redteam.result (verdict unable_to_verify); no expectation_gap output in the run
findings.fix: After the capital bridge is fixed (see review_numbers), declare revenue_basis, reinvestment (capex/revenue), funding need, SBC treatment and backlog use. Run redteam_audit and expectation_gap with each lever alone (growth, margin, sales_to_capital), and show the result as a draft until both pass.

findings.finding: The falsifiers do not test the crux. All five are revenue, ARR or MW milestones that measure management's plan. None tests returns or funding, which are where the thesis fails: margin after depreciation, price per MW, dilution, refinancing. No falsifier covers the key risk (dilution or funding), and the bear has a single falsifier. The bull falsifier (contracted power below 5,000 MW by 2026-12-31) tests management's own target, not the bull's 20% return.
findings.where: position/core.json falsifiers (fx_rev26, fx_arr26, fx_mw26, fx_cpower26, fx_bear_rev27)
findings.fix: Add numeric dated falsifiers. Base: AI cloud adjusted EBITDA margin below 45% in FY2027, or GAAP operating margin not positive by Q4 2027 (checked 2028-03-31). Key risk: diluted shares above about 330M at 2027-12-31, or the Citi facility not refinanced by 2027-10-22. Bull: new contracts below 20M USD per MW per year in 2027. Bear: FY2027 operating margin above 10% refutes the bear.

findings.finding: One bear event has no evidence. 'GPU-hour price falls as supply grows and demand moves to inference, and the operating margin stays in single digits' is labelled hypothesis with no ids, yet it is the bear's main margin mechanism (mature_margin 0.08). The bull event of the first auction clearing 15% above Blackwell rests on management's call only (dc_call_q2, a provider-normalized transcript with no saved payload).
findings.fix: Cite a dated GPU rental price series or CoreWeave's disclosed pricing or margin trend for the bear price mechanism, or keep it as a hypothesis and say the bear margin is a judgement. Corroborate the auction claim from the Q2 6-K or a release.

findings.finding: The path labels are honest but untestable: all three are 'unproven', with own_history and peers left out (EPS negative through FY2027 on consensus). Volatility is not mistaken for business risk, and no peer median is used, but the bull leans on Token Factory software pricing (field.json), a minor revenue line with no disclosed revenue share.
findings.where: position/path.json gaps; position/field.json bull reading (Token Factory)
findings.fix: State the Token Factory revenue share, or drop it as a bull support until it is disclosed.
